newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK composites Q1 to benefit from weather.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK composites Q1 to benefit from weather.

text.p: Two British composite insurers reporting results next week are expected to show a robust performance over the first three months of the year.
In particular, comparisons are likely to be helped by the much more favourable winter weather experienced over the quarter.
Scottish-based General Accident will report results on Tuesday followed by Commercial Union on Wednesday.

General Accident has already said at its annual meeting that it expects the better weather conditions in Britain and North America will result in "much improved" first quarter results compared with last year.
Then pre-tax operating profit fell to 55 million stg from 112 million stg the previous year after weather claims cost it 70 million stg.
Salomon Brothers is forecasting pre-tax profits for the quarter to rise by 70 percent to 94 million stg while Lehman Brothers expects profits of 103 million stg and Merrill Lynch 108 million stg.
In March, General Accident sold its New Zealand life company to Prudential Corp for around 70 million stg as part of its strategy to concentrate its life and pensions business in Britain.

At the company's annual results earlier in the month, chief executive Bob Scott described market conditions as "increasingly competitive" although he was hopeful of a rise in motor premiums this year.
Commercial Union has also said it expects to report "a good increase" in profits for the first quarter compared with 1996.

Chief executive John Carter told the annual meeting in April that its businesses were developing in line with plans and that in particular the group was seeing another strong increase in new life business.
He added that results would get a boost from the mild winter weather in the northern hemisphere including North America.
The company has already reported a rise in new life, pensions and investment sales of 25 percent to 853 million stg in the first quarter.
Growth was strong in Italy and Poland and the UK with a solid performance in Holland. However, analysts said that the UK was heavily dependent on single premiums and France was sharply lower.
Salomon Brothers forecasts results to show modest progress on the 83 million stg reported last year.
It expects the heavy exposure to French and Dutch life assurance profits and the bias of the non-life investment portfolio to overseas markets to depress profits because of the strength of sterling.
Salomon's forecast of 93 million stg for the quarter compares with Lehman's 101 million stg and Merrril's 115 million stg.
At its annual results in February, Commercial Union said it intended to continue to expand its life operations to take advantage of its more consistent profit streams and "exciting" growth prospects.

In April, the company took its share of the French life market to around 4.5 percent with the acquisition of 73.1 percent of SEV ("Societe d'Epargne Viagere"), a French life assurer, and 100 percent of a French insurance broking business from Compagnie de Suez.
The move takes the overall group's business split between life and general insurance to 50:50 based on 1996 pro forma numbers for 1996.
The company said at the time of the deal it expected it to be earnings enhancing in the first year.
-- Simon Cowell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7721
